s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological decline with mass effect and subsequent respiratory decompensation
salient_findings: Ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe
Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF
New left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence on chest radiograph
key_facts: 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI showed a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes)
Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
Fever to 39.6 °C
Generalized weakness
1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification
CT scan of the chest confirmed extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL, respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings consistent with opportunistic infection

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL, respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings consistent with opportunistic infection

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL, respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings consistent with opportunistic fungal infection

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute neurological decline with mass effect, HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL

raw.rationale: The patient's MRI showed a ring-enhancing lesion, and CSF studies were positive for toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii, with histopathologic examination revealing bradyzoites and tachyzoites, all of which are diagnostic of toxoplasmosis, particularly in the context of a severely immunocompromised patient with HIV infection and a very low CD4 count.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient has a low CD4 count and presents with respiratory symptoms, the initial diagnosis of toxoplasmosis and the specific findings in the brain tissue do not directly support this diagnosis as the primary cause of the current presentation.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence provided in the vignette that supports CMV pneumonia, such as positive CMV PCR in the blood or respiratory secretions.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and the findings on the chest radiograph and CT scan could suggest a fungal infection, but the initial workup and treatment focused on toxoplasmosis and bacterial infections, with no specific evidence provided for invasive aspergillosis.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: The histopathologic examination revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites, which are indicative of toxoplasmosis, not lymphoma, and the patient's clinical presentation and response to treatment for toxoplasmosis do not support this diagnosis.
